skill.name: bid-on-profit
skill.description: Set up and check POAS (profit on ad spend) or ROAS bidding with Product Metrics in Google Ads and Meta: confirm the profit conversion actions exist, additional costs are active, the right action is primary, and the target ROAS fits the value sent. Use it when someone asks to "bid on profit", "switch to POAS", "use Product Metrics - Profit", "what target ROAS should I use", or why profit conversions are empty or zero. Uses the productmetrics CLI or the Product Metrics MCP server for the checks; making an action primary and setting a target ROAS are steps the person does in Google Ads or Meta.
skill.summary: Check Product Metrics conversion tracking and plan profit or revenue bidding changes in Google Ads and Meta.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The static alerts cover Markdown formatting, product documentation links, and read-only Product Metrics account checks. The skill directs agents to create missing conversion actions through another skill without stating an approval requirement. No evidence of prompt injection, host reconnaissance, or unauthorized data transfer was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: Conversion action creation is suggested without an explicit approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Keep checks read-only by default. Confirm the advertiser, store, and intended secondary conversion action before calling any tool that creates it.

content.user_title: Check Profit and Revenue Bidding Setup
content.value_statement: Bidding on the wrong conversion value can favor sales that do not cover advertising costs. Review your Product Metrics setup and plan changes for Google Ads or Meta.
actual_capabilities: Identify the store and inspect linked Google Ads conversion actions and their reported goal status.
Guide a manual check of additional costs and product cost fallback settings.
Show campaign POAS and products that lose money after advertising through connected Product Metrics MCP tools.
Suggest a starting Google Ads target from the current POAS or ROAS and verify goal status after a manual change.
Check the configured Meta destination and explain how an advertiser can select a profit conversion.
limitations: Live checks require access to the Product Metrics CLI or MCP server. Campaign and product profitability reports require MCP.
There is no costs API in this workflow. Users check and update additional costs in Product Metrics.
Users must change primary conversion goals, bidding targets, and Meta optimization events in the ad platforms themselves.
Search and Demand Gen POAS estimates use the account average margin, not campaign-specific margins.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Conversion Action
prompt_templates.prompt: For my selected store, tell me whether Product Metrics - Profit exists and whether Google Ads reports it as primary. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Profit Conversions
prompt_templates.prompt: My profit conversions are missing or zero. Explain what I should check in Tracking and which symptoms can reflect missing costs or unprofitable orders.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Profit Bidding Pilot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the connected POAS report to suggest a starting Google Ads target for one campaign. Mark estimated values and list the manual steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Profitability Across Channels
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare campaign POAS and flag products losing money after ads. Check the Meta destination and separate verified setup details from recommendations. Do not make changes.

output_examples.input: My Google Ads campaign has a POAS of 1.5. What target should I start with?
output: For a campaign bidding on profit, start near a 150% target ROAS. A 100% target represents break-even on ad spend.
Test one campaign first. In Google Ads, make the profit action primary and set the old purchase action to secondary for the relevant goal.
Switching conversion value can reset what Google Ads has learned about that value.

output_examples.input: The profit action is linked but has no conversions. What should I check?
output: In Product Metrics, open Tracking and check whether additional costs are active.
Verify that each order line has a product cost or that a fallback percentage is set. Orders with unknown costs send revenue only.
A zero profit value is different from a missing conversion. Product Metrics sends losses as zero.

best_practices: Confirm the intended store and use the company and property identifiers returned by Product Metrics.
Pilot a change in one campaign and verify the conversion goal status after the advertiser makes it.
Check additional costs before switching to profit and label estimated POAS in reports.
anti_patterns: Reusing a revenue target unchanged when switching to profit as the conversion value.
Leaving both purchase actions primary for the same bidding goal.
Treating a zero profit value as proof that cost tracking is incomplete.

faq.question: What is the difference between POAS and ROAS?
faq.answer: POAS divides profit by ad spend. ROAS divides revenue by ad spend.

faq.question: Why does Google Ads still call the target ROAS?
faq.answer: Google Ads uses the target ROAS label for conversion value. With a profit conversion action, a 150% target corresponds to a POAS of 1.5.

faq.question: Can the skill change what my campaigns bid on?
faq.answer: No. You make conversion goal, target, and optimization event changes in Google Ads or Meta.

faq.question: Why are some profit conversions zero?
faq.answer: Product Metrics sends losses as zero. Missing or inactive costs can cause a missing profit conversion instead.

faq.question: When is campaign POAS estimated?
faq.answer: For Search and Demand Gen campaigns, Product Metrics estimates POAS using the account average margin.

faq.question: When can I compare new and old conversion actions?
faq.answer: Product Metrics Home shows a collecting status and compares the actions 14 days after the first order.
